Ben / Alicia —

Thanks for the thread. Quick summary of Redwood's preferred position and a few options to help break the logjam. I'm copying the relevant snippet language below (for insertion into the MSA order of precedence immediately after the dispute resolution section).

Summary (Redwood position):
- Governing law: State of California, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- Forum: Exclusive state or federal courts located in San Francisco County for actions seeking equitable relief; arbitration remains the default for claims seeking monetary damages.
- Equitable relief carveout: Mutual carveout allowing either party to seek injunctive or other equitable relief in court without waiving right to arbitrate other claims.
- Tolling / notice: Parties should provide written notice and a 7-business-day cure/engagement period for commercially reasonable remediation and executive escalation before filing for injunctive relief, but such tolling will not be a condition precedent to seeking emergency relief where irreparable harm is imminent.

Suggested redline snippets (pick one):

Option A (clean, narrow carveout — recommended):
"Notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional or preliminary injunctive relief, including temporary restraining orders, in any state or federal court of competent jurisdiction located in San Francisco County, California, to prevent the actual or threatened misappropriation or disclosure of Confidential Information or infringement of Intellectual Property. The institution of such court proceedings shall not constitute a waiver of any right to demand arbitration with respect to other disputes between the parties."

Option B (compromise for neutral forum):
"The parties agree that, notwithstanding an agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek provisional or preliminary injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction located in the State of Delaware or the State of California where such relief is necessary to prevent the unauthorized disclosure of Confidential Information or infringement of Intellectual Property. The parties will, to the extent practicable, provide written notice and engage in senior-executive escalation for up to seven (7) business days prior to filing for such relief, except where immediate relief is necessary to prevent irreparable harm."

Tolling note: Novum requested a 10-day tolling window — Redwood views 7 business days as operationally realistic; if Novum needs 10 calendar days we can take that to execs for commercial trade-offs.

Operational guarantees: we can commit to an expedited meet-and-confer and provide a named Redwood escalation contact in the order form; our legal team will prioritize briefing deadlines and share an initial proposed temporary relief declaration template (short affidavit) to streamline emergency filings.

Attachments: I'm attaching a two-page excerpt (RWI_recommendation_excerpt.pdf) with the preferred snippet plus a very brief fallback compromise language for arbitration administrators.

Next steps: Alicia — tell me whether Option A or Option B is closer to Novum's appetite. If you'd like the hybrid (CA law + Delaware forum) please flag — that combination introduces a conflict risk we should discuss and would likely need an executive exception. If Novum prefers Option B with a 10-day tolling window, Ben: please advise whether Redwood commercial can accept a slightly longer tolling window in exchange for Redwood retaining CA law.

Happy to jump on a short call later today or tomorrow (I have availability 3–5pm PT).

Best,
